findings.title: reset callback exact range and cleared slots
findings.detail: src/routes/roster/+page.svelte:116-164 (the `reset: ({ isSwitch }) => { ... },` property passed to createRouteLoadMachine). Clears: reorderError (121), reorderStatus (122), removeError (128), pendingRemoveId (129), pendingDeactivateId (132), deactivateRefusal (133), deactivateActionError (134), recordEditorMemberId (143), recordEditorLookup (144), recordSaveError (145), recordStatus (151), and inside `if (isSwitch) {...}` (159-163): showInactive (160), inactiveRows (161), inactiveLoadError (162). Confirmed by full-file grep for `removePending`/`deactivatePending` (declared at :1600 and :787 respectively) that neither identifier appears anywhere in lines 116-164 — both are absent from the reset callback, matching prior research at current HEAD (6fe8556).

findings.title: route-load machine module and generation mechanics
findings.detail: Machine lives in src/lib/loading/routeLoad.ts (createRouteLoadMachine, :83). `generation` is a plain closure counter (`let generation = 0;` at :86), incremented unconditionally at the top of every loadForSelected() call (`const g = ++generation;` at :96) — never $state, never mutated by a read. Exposed to callers as a non-mutating getter `routeLoad.generation` (:136-138) and a helper `routeLoad.isCurrent(g)` (:90-92, :139) that returns `g === generation`. Two equivalent compare idioms are both live on the roster page: `if (!routeLoad.isCurrent(g)) return;` (e.g. +page.svelte:951,954, inside handleDeactivateConfirm's inactive-panel reload) and `if (g !== routeLoad.generation) return;` (e.g. +page.svelte:1702, inside handleRemoveSection's post-failure reconcile, and repeated at :2123,2135,2253,2258,2293,2454 for reorder/reparent). Either is the reusable idiom per module doc comment at routeLoad.ts:17-20.

findings.title: confirmed un-guarded finally blocks and un-guarded success-path live-region writes
findings.detail: deactivatePending: finally block at +page.svelte:968-982; the flag reset `deactivatePending = false;` at :969 is unconditional — no isCurrent/generation check (the nearby guard at :951/:954 only protects the inner inactive-panel-reload settle, not the finally itself). removePending: finally block at +page.svelte:1716-1719; `removePending = false;` at :1717 is unconditional, despite the adjacent reconcile branch (:1700-1708) being generation-guarded. Success-path live-region write `removeStatus = m.roster_section_removed({ name });` at :1684 is also written unconditionally in the try block, before any generation check — this is the un-guarded cross-collective announcement risk #287 targets.

Other *Pending flags exist on the page (reorderPending, renamePending, reinstatePending, recordSavingMemberId — the last deliberately excluded from reset per comment at :146-150) that were not checked for the same reset-callback/generation-guard gap; per the issue's scope fence, any such gap found later belongs in its own issue, not folded into #287.

findings.title: removePending — declaration, set-true, set-false (all at HEAD)
findings.detail: Declaration: src/routes/roster/+page.svelte:1600 `let removePending = $state(false);`. Set true: :1659 `removePending = true;` (first statement inside the `try` block, i.e. after `removeError = null;` and `removeStatus = '';` reset but before `await deleteSection(cfg, id);`). Set false: :1717 `removePending = false;` — the FIRST statement of the `finally` block. There are no other assignments to `removePending` anywhere in the file (verified by exhaustive grep for `removePending = `).

findings.title: Enclosing handler: handleRemoveSection, full try/catch/finally (quoted, current line numbers)
findings.detail:
`async function handleRemoveSection(id: string): Promise<void>` starts at :1602. Structure at HEAD:

:1608 `if (structuralWritePending) return;` — early single-flight guard, BEFORE removePending is set.
:1612-1620 — `fallbackId`, `active`, `ownsFocus` computed (pre-mutation, synchronous).
:1632 `removeError = null;`
:1635 `removeStatus = '';`
:1636-1637 — `name`, `cfg = currentCfg`.
:1638-1643 — `if (!cfg) { ...; removeError = {...}; if (ownsFocus) await placeFocusAfterFailedRemove(id); return; }` — an EARLY RETURN before the generation is even captured and before `removePending` is set. This path never touches `removePending` at all (leaves it however it already was — always false here since nothing upstream sets it before this point) and is NOT inside the try/finally.
:1647 `const g = routeLoad.generation;`
:1648 `const before = sections;`
:1658 `let failedRemoveId: string | null = null;`
:1659 `removePending = true;`
:1660 `try {`
  :1661 `await deleteSection(cfg, id);`
  :1668 `sections = removeSectionNode(sections, id);`
  :1670 `pendingRemoveId = null;`
  :1679-1683 — prune `expandedIds` if present.
  :1684 `removeStatus = m.roster_section_removed({ name });`
  :1685 `if (ownsFocus) await placeFocusAfterRemove(fallbackId);`
:1686 `} catch (e) {`
  :1687 `console.error('roster: section remove failed', id, e);`
  :1700 `try {`
    :1701 `const fresh = await listSections(cfg);`
    :1702 `if (g !== routeLoad.generation) return; // superseded by a newer collective selection`
    :1703 `sections = fresh;`
  :1704 `} catch (refetchError) {`
    :1705 `console.error('roster: section refetch after a failed remove failed', refetchError);`
    :1706 `if (g !== routeLoad.generation) return;`
    :1707 `sections = before;`
  :1708 `}`
  :1712 `removeError = { name, kind: isSectionNotEmpty(e) ? 'not-empty' : 'write' };`
  :1713 `failedRemoveId = id;`
:1716 `} finally {`
  :1717 `removePending = false;`
  :1718 `if (ownsFocus && failedRemoveId !== null) await placeFocusAfterFailedRemove(failedRemoveId);`
:1719 `}`
:1720 `}` (end of function)

Note: BOTH `return` statements inside the catch's nested try/catch (:1702, :1706) return from those INNER try/catch blocks only in effect for reconcile logic, but since there is no code after the inner try/catch within the outer `catch` block other than `removeError`/`failedRemoveId` assignment, an early `return` at :1702 or :1706 actually returns from the WHOLE async function `handleRemoveSection` — which SKIPS the outer `finally` entirely in JS/TS semantics? No — `finally` always runs even on `return` from within `try`/`catch`, including nested returns, per JS semantics. So :1717 `removePending = false` and the un-guarded focus call at :1718 DO still execute even when :1702 or :1706 fire, despite the generation having already changed. This confirms the bug: the two generation checks at :1702/:1706 stop the `sections`/tree mutation but do NOT stop `finally` from clearing `removePending` (:1717) or, when `failedRemoveId` was never set on those early-return paths (it's still null, set only at :1713 which is skipped by the :1702/:1706 returns), from doing anything with the stale id — HOWEVER `failedRemoveId` stays null on those two early-return paths so :1718's focus call is skipped safely; the surviving un-guarded write is `removePending = false` at :1717 itself, which un-disables the NEW collective's structural controls (`structuralWritePending`) as a side effect of a removal that belonged to the OLD collective.

findings.title: Generation checks already inside handleRemoveSection
findings.detail: Exactly two, both inside the `catch` block's nested reconcile try/catch, both quoted above: :1702 `if (g !== routeLoad.generation) return; // superseded by a newer collective selection` and :1706 `if (g !== routeLoad.generation) return;`. `g` is captured once at :1647 (`const g = routeLoad.generation;`), AFTER the `!cfg` early-return at :1638-1643 and BEFORE `removePending = true` at :1659. There is no generation check anywhere in the success branch (:1661-1685) and none in the `finally` (:1716-1719) — confirming the prior research's claim that the `finally` is un-guarded.

findings.title: Live-region / status writes on success and failure paths
findings.detail:
SUCCESS path — :1684 `removeStatus = m.roster_section_removed({ name });` where `name` was captured at :1636 `const name = findSectionNode(sections, id)?.name ?? id;` (looked up BEFORE the write starts, from the tree that was on screen when the removal was armed — i.e. whichever collective was current at that point, not necessarily the collective current when this line executes). Rendered at :3643-3648: `
{removeStatus}
`. FAILURE path (cfg-missing early return) — :1640 `removeError = { name, kind: 'write' };` where `name` is again the pre-capture from :1636. FAILURE path (catch block) — :1712 `removeError = { name, kind: isSectionNotEmpty(e) ? 'not-empty' : 'write' };`. Both render via :3752-3762: `{#if removeError}

{removeError.kind === 'not-empty' ? m.roster_section_remove_not_empty({ name: removeError.name }) : m.roster_section_remove_failed({ name: removeError.name })}

{/if}`. Neither :1684 (success) nor :1640/:1712 (failure) is guarded by a `g !== routeLoad.generation` check — all three can fire after a collective switch and will name a section from the PRIOR collective (via the pre-captured `name` closure variable) into the CURRENT collective's live region / alert, which is exactly the cross-collective-announcement defect #287 describes.

findings.title: structuralWritePending — definition and every consumer
findings.detail:
Definition at :2393: `const structuralWritePending = $derived(reorderPending || renamePending || removePending);` (preceded by an explanatory comment block at :2381-2392 not reproduced here in full).

Functional (JS logic) consumers — each an `if (structuralWritePending) return...` early-return guard:
:1608 inside `handleRemoveSection` itself.
:2098 inside `performReorder`.
:2221 inside `performReparent`.
:2396 inside `startRename`.
:2425 inside `submitRename`.
:2698 inside `handlePointerDown`.
:2868 inside `toggleGrab`.

Template (render-site) consumers, all inside the arrange-row markup for a given `row`/`node`:
:4105 `draggable={structuralWritePending || damaged ? 'false' : 'true'}` on the draggable row.
:4109 (same class-string ternary, `cursor-default` vs `cursor-grab`) on the row's class list.
:4160 grip handle `class="... {structuralWritePending ? 'cursor-default' : 'cursor-grab hover:...'}"`.
:4196 rename-trigger button `disabled={structuralWritePending || renamingSectionId === row.id}`.
:4316 indent button `disabled={structuralWritePending || renamingSectionId === row.id || damaged || !indentApplicable}`.
:4335 unindent button `disabled={structuralWritePending || renamingSectionId === row.id || damaged || !unindentApplicable}`.
:4389 remove-confirm button `disabled={structuralWritePending}` (paired with `aria-busy={removePending}` on the SAME button, :4390 — i.e. `removePending` also has a direct, non-`structuralWritePending`-mediated consumer here).
:4400 remove-cancel button `disabled={structuralWritePending}`.
:4419-4421 `DeleteTrigger` (the ✕ trigger that arms remove) `disabled={structuralWritePending || renamingSectionId === row.id || !canDelete}`.

All of the above are gated on `structuralWritePending` as a WHOLE-PAGE derived flag (not scoped to the row/section that owns the in-flight write), so as long as `removePending` stays true — including across a collective switch, since neither `removePending` nor its declaration site is touched by the `reset` callback — every one of these controls for EVERY row on the NEW collective's tree stays disabled/non-draggable. This is the (a) half of #287.

findings.title: Confirmed: reset() callback does not clear removePending or removeStatus
findings.detail: The route-load machine's `reset: ({ isSwitch }) => { ... }` callback spans :116-164. It clears `reorderError`/`reorderStatus` (:121-122), `removeError`/`pendingRemoveId` (:128-129), the deactivate trio `pendingDeactivateId`/`deactivateRefusal`/`deactivateActionError` (:132-134), the record-editor trio (:143-145), `recordStatus` (:151), and (isSwitch-gated) `showInactive`/`inactiveRows`/`inactiveLoadError` (:159-163). It does NOT reference `removePending` or `removeStatus` anywhere in that span — confirmed by reading the full callback body and by the earlier grep showing `removePending = ` has exactly the three sites already listed (none inside `reset`). This matches PRIOR RESEARCH's claim and remains true at HEAD despite line drift (was ~124/127-129 in #273-era research; is now :129/:132-134 for the sibling flags that ARE cleared, with removePending/removeStatus still absent).

findings.title: Enclosing handler: handleDeactivateConfirm — full try/catch/finally quoted
Existing generation checks — confirmed: only the inactive-panel reload sub-branch is guarded
Live-region / status writes on the deactivate paths
findings.detail:
There is NO success live-region announcement for deactivate at all — verified by grepping every `role="status"`/`aria-live` region in the file (:3611-3687, :3771-3783): they cover reorder (`reorderStatus`), section-remove (`removeStatus`), section-create (`pageCreateStatus`), rename (`renameStatus`), and member-record-save (`recordStatus`) — none is `deactivateStatus` or equivalent. On a successful deactivate the member simply disappears from the roster via the `loadForSelected()` re-render; no message names the action performed, so there is no cross-collective mis-announcement vector on the SUCCESS path (nothing to mis-announce). Failure/refusal paths use `role="alert"` elements, both keyed per-row and gated on `pendingDeactivateId === row.memberId` in their `{#if}` (so a reset `pendingDeactivateId`, cleared unconditionally by the route-load `reset` callback at :132, structurally prevents these two alerts from surviving a collective switch even without touching `deactivatePending`): - Refusal: `:3481` `{#if pendingDeactivateId === row.memberId && deactivateRefusal?.memberId === row.memberId}` → `

` (:3490-3500), text from `m.roster_deactivate_refused_admin({collective})` / `m.roster_deactivate_refused_librarian({collective})` (:3496-3498). - Failure: `:3502` `{#if pendingDeactivateId === row.memberId && deactivateActionError?.memberId === row.memberId && deactivateActionError.kind === 'deactivate'}` → `

` (:3510-3516), text `m.roster_member_deactivate_failed({ name: row.profileName ?? row.name })` (:3515). So the concrete #287 gap for `deactivatePending` is narrower than for `removePending`: it is not that a stale message could NAME the wrong collective's action (no such message exists), but that `deactivatePending = false` firing ungated in the `finally` after a collective switch leaves the STRUCTURAL CONTROLS (confirm/cancel/trigger buttons, all three `disabled={deactivatePending}`) re-enabled based on a write that belonged to the OLD collective, exactly mirroring the `removePending` bug shape at the control-disable level even though there is no matching live-region-copy half of the bug for this flag.

findings.detail:
Read/checked (not counting comments):

  - :869 `handleDeactivateConfirm`: `if (deactivatePending) return;` — re-entrancy guard.

findings.title: The #260 idiom, canonical shape, quoted verbatim
Capture-before-await / compare-after-await mechanics
findings.detail:
Every site captures `g = routeLoad.generation` SYNCHRONOUSLY, before the first `await` of the operation it guards, then compares `g` against the (possibly-advanced) live `routeLoad.generation` immediately after each subsequent await, before any state write. Two capture-timing subtleties recur across the roster page's sites:

1. When the guarded operation is itself triggered BY a call to `loadForSelected()` (which bumps `generation` unconditionally), the capture must happen AFTER that call, not at function entry — otherwise the guard reads stale on every ordinary (non-superseded) run and silently no-ops. Documented explicitly at roster/+page.svelte:941-946 (deactivate's inactive-panel reload) and :1007-1011 (reinstate's mirror): 'Captured HERE, after `loadForSelected()` above, not at function entry: that call bumps the generation unconditionally, so an entry-captured guard would already read stale and silently skip this refresh on every ORDINARY deactivate/reinstate with the panel open.'
2. When the guarded operation does NOT call `loadForSelected()` itself (remove/reorder/rename's own write-then-reconcile), `g` is captured once at the top of the handler and reused across both the success branch and the catch/refetch branch — see roster/+page.svelte:1647 (reparent), :2106 (reorder), :2229 (renumber), :2435 (tree refresh).

findings.title: Complete current-site inventory in roster/+page.svelte
findings.detail: All current uses of routeLoad.generation / routeLoad.isCurrent in src/routes/roster/+page.svelte (grep -n "generation\|isCurrent" on 2026-09-08, post-#285/#286): the route-load body's own `isCurrent()` check (:190); the deactivate-confirm inactive-panel reload (:947,951,954); the reinstate inactive-panel reload (:1007,1012,1016,1019); the record-editor open (:1202,1208,1242); the record-editor save (:1349,1367,1369,1417,1423); performReparent's reconcile (:1647,1697,1702,1706); performReorder's reconcile including the #264-added success-path guard (:2106,2123,2135,2139); the renumber/reorder-duplicate path (:2229,2253,2258,2293,2297); and a tree refresh (:2435,2454,2458). This is a hand-rolled idiom repeated at every site — there is NO shared helper function that wraps 'capture g, await, compare, conditionally write.' Only the two primitives (`generation` getter, `isCurrent(g)` method) are shared, from `createRouteLoadMachine` in src/lib/loading/routeLoad.ts. Each call site writes its own `if (g !== routeLoad.generation) return;` / `if (!routeLoad.isCurrent(g)) return;` line by hand.

findings.title: removePending and deactivatePending currently use NEITHER half of the idiom
findings.detail:
Confirmed against current source (line numbers re-verified 2026-09-08, drifted from the #273-era research as expected):

- `deactivatePending` ($state, declared roster/+page.svelte:787) is set true at :884 and cleared unconditionally in the `finally` at :969 (`deactivatePending = false;` — no generation check). It is NOT touched anywhere in the shared `reset()` callback (roster/+page.svelte:116-163, which the route-load machine runs synchronously at the top of every `loadForSelected()`, per routeLoad.ts:97). Note: the deactivate flow DOES already use the #260 idiom, but only for its own inactive-panel reload sub-branch (:947-954) — the boolean flag itself is outside that guard.
- `removePending` ($state, declared :1600) is set true at :1659 and cleared unconditionally in the `finally` at :1717 (`removePending = false;` — no generation check). Also absent from `reset()`. The handler DOES capture `const g = routeLoad.generation;` at :1647, and uses it correctly to guard the catch-branch reconcile (`listSections` refetch, :1697-1706) — but that same already-captured `g` is never consulted in the `finally`.

So the fix does not need to invent a new capture — `handleDeactivateConfirm` needs its OWN `g` capture near the top (mirroring :947's placement/reasoning, since it also calls `loadForSelected()` internally and must capture after that call per the timing rule above), and `handleRemoveSection` already has `g` in scope at :1647 and only needs the `finally` at :1717 to consult it.

findings.title: Precise shape the fix should take (reuse, not reinvent)
findings.detail:
Two independent changes, both direct reuses of the existing idiom:

1. **Reset on switch** — add `removePending = false;` and `deactivatePending = false;` to the `reset()` callback (roster/+page.svelte:116-163), alongside the sibling state each flag's own two-step-confirm already resets there (`pendingRemoveId` at :129 / `pendingDeactivateId` at :132). This is the SAME reset() the machine already runs synchronously before every load (routeLoad.ts:97) — no new mechanism, just adding the two missing lines to an existing list. This fixes 'disabled from load': a switch to B must not inherit A's in-flight flag.
2. **Generation-guard the finally** — change `finally { removePending = false; ... }` (:1717) to only clear when still current: `finally { if (routeLoad.isCurrent(g)) removePending = false; ...focus logic, which is already itself keyed to `pendingRemoveId === row...`/ownsFocus and should likely also stay generation-gated... }`, using the `g` already captured at :1647. Same pattern for `deactivatePending`'s finally (:969), after adding a `const g = routeLoad.generation;` capture placed AFTER the flow's own `loadForSelected()` call (:892 area) per the capture-timing rule in finding 2 — mirroring exactly how :947 already captures `g` in this same function for the inactive-panel reload. This fixes the reverse race: A's stale settle must not flip a flag that by then legitimately reflects B's own in-flight write.

3. **Gap the two-flag scope does NOT close (must be named, per the issue's own instruction, not silently fixed here):** the success-path write `removeStatus = m.roster_section_removed({ name })` at roster/+page.svelte:1684 (inside the `try`, before the `finally`) is UNGUARDED by generation — a delete confirmed on A that settles after a switch to B will still announce A's section name into B's live region, independent of whatever `removePending` does. This is exactly the bug class #264 already fixed for reorder's success path — compare roster/+page.svelte:2118-2124, which added `if (g !== routeLoad.generation) return false; // superseded by a newer collective selection` immediately before writing `reorderStatus`, with the commit-message-documented rationale 'a SUCCESS settling after a collective switch must write NOTHING for the stale collective... the #259/#260 class.' `handleRemoveSection`'s success branch needs the identical guard before its `removeStatus` write (and arguably before the `sections = removeSectionNode(...)` mutation and `pendingRemoveId = null` on the same lines, :1677-1684) to satisfy the issue's own done-when #3 ('a live-region announcement can never name an action performed in a different collective'). `deactivatePending`'s flow has no equivalent unguarded live-region write — it has no dedicated success-status string; its only post-write announcement risk (`deactivateActionError`) is already row-scoped and read-guarded by `pendingDeactivateId === row.memberId` at the render site, so no analogous gap exists there.

findings.title: Other pending flags on the roster page sharing the same two gaps (name-only, per scope fence — do not fix here)
findings.detail:
Neither of these is `removePending`/`deactivatePending`, but both show the identical pattern of (a) absent from `reset()` and (b) an unguarded `finally`, so the issue's own instruction to 'NAME them' rather than fold them in applies:

- `reorderPending` (declared :2027) — set true at :2107 and :2230, cleared unconditionally in `finally` at :2142 and :2300; not present in `reset()`. Its live-region write (`reorderStatus`) IS already generation-guarded (the #264 fix, :2118-2124), so only the flag-clearing gap remains here, not the announcement gap.
- `renamePending` (declared :2367) — set true at :2437, cleared unconditionally in `finally` at :2463; not present in `reset()`. Its live-region write `renameStatus = m.roster_section_renamed(...)` at :2441 is ALSO unguarded (no #264-style fix was ever applied to rename) — so rename carries all three gaps at once (flag-reset, finally-guard, live-region).
- `reinstatePending` (declared :1038, typed `string | null` — a memberId, not a boolean) — set at :1044, cleared unconditionally at :1076; not present in `reset()`.

For contrast, `recordSavingMemberId` (:1135) is explicitly documented (comment at :146-150) as DELIBERATELY not reset on switch, and its `finally` at :1448 uses a DIFFERENT but structurally sound guard: `if (recordSavingMemberId === memberId) recordSavingMemberId = null;` — an identity comparison rather than the generation comparison, valid here because it's a per-row flag keyed to a globally-unique Entu member id rather than a page-wide boolean, so a stale settle from a different row (or a different collective's differently-id'd member) cannot false-clear it. This is a deliberate precedent for a member-id-keyed guard being an acceptable alternative shape to the generation guard for row-scoped (not page-scoped) pending state — not itself in need of the #287 fix.

findings.title: Confirmed bug mechanics — reset() gap and un-guarded finally blocks
findings.detail: reset callback src/routes/roster/+page.svelte:116-164 clears pendingRemoveId(129)/removeError(128) and pendingDeactivateId(132)/deactivateRefusal(133)/deactivateActionError(134) but never touches removePending (declared :1600, set true :1659) or deactivatePending (declared :787, set true :884). handleRemoveSection's finally (:1716-1719) unconditionally sets removePending=false with no routeLoad.generation check. handleDeactivateConfirm's finally (:968-982) unconditionally sets deactivatePending=false with no generation check — note the finally does not even run until the panel-reload sub-await at :950 (which IS generation-guarded, :951/:954) settles, since that await is nested inside the same outer try. structuralWritePending derives at :2393 as `reorderPending || renamePending || removePending` (page-wide). removeStatus (the live-region success announcement) is set unconditionally at :1684 with NO generation check on the success path at all (only the failure/refetch branches at :1700-1708 are guarded) — this is the literal 'announces A's removal into B's live region' mechanism named in the issue.

findings.title: The house generation-guard idiom to reuse is #260's (profile page), and it is ALREADY applied elsewhere on this same page for structural-write success branches
findings.detail: git show 01ed068 (fix #260, src/routes/profile/+page.svelte) is the canonical idiom: capture `g = generation` before the async op, and at settle `if (g !== generation) return` before writing ANY state (value or error) — a stale settle writes nothing. On the roster page, performReorder (:2090-2145) and performReparent (:2213-2303) already apply this to their SUCCESS branches (:2123, :2253, :2258) and their refetch-reconcile branches (:1702/1706, :2135, :2293/2297) — but critically their own `finally` blocks (:2141-2143, :2299-2301) are UNGUARDED too, same gap class as removePending/deactivatePending. submitRename's finally (:2462-2463) is likewise unguarded. Since the issue's scope fence is 'THESE TWO FLAGS ONLY', reorderPending's and renamePending's un-guarded finally blocks are the SAME gap but out of scope — naming them per the scope-fence instruction rather than fixing them.

findings.title: PRIMARY blast radius #1 — page.roster-arrange-crud.spec.ts (section-remove flow, single-collective)
findings.detail: 1157 lines, the file most tied to removePending/structuralWritePending-gated controls. Every `it` block relevant to the fix (none currently exercise a collective switch — `grep -n 'switch|generation' page.roster-arrange-crud.spec.ts` returns nothing): describe ':318 DELETE in Arrange mode ALWAYS rendered, DISABLED when ineligible' (:319-380, disabled-state assertions unrelated to pending, low risk); describe ':474 arrange-mode structural writes are SINGLE-FLIGHT (#155/S4 review F1)' — `:475` asserts rename/indent/unindent DISABLED on other rows and `draggable=false` while a delete is in flight (reads structuralWritePending indirectly through rendered attributes), `:500` same for reparent, `:524` reorder-pending clears on failure too; describe ':607 delete outcome ANNOUNCED (#155/S4 review F5)' — `:608` SUCCESS announces into roster-section-remove-status (reads removeStatus, the exact un-guarded live region), `:628` FAILED raises section-remove-error, `:651` REFUSED (not-empty) gets its own message; describe ':680 keyboard contract' — `:685` successful-delete focus landing, `:728` failed-delete leaves pair armed+focus, `:764` refused-delete keeps pair armed; describe ':881 #237 trashcan render' — `:908`/`:921` disabled-state + two-step through the swap; describe ':963 #273 armed pair through in-flight delete' — `:964` confirm starts write without unmounting (both halves disabled/aria-busy, no double-fire), `:1004` CANCEL mid-flight inert, `:1048` SUCCESS clears armed id, `:1077` FAILURE leaves pair armed, `:1135` 'the KNOWN-GAP comments … are removed with the fix' (a literal marker test for a prior fix's cleanup — check whether an analogous marker convention is wanted for #287). ALL of these are single-collective and assert removePending's CURRENT correct in-flight/failure/success behavior within one collective — they are not asserting the cross-collective leak (nothing here switches collectives), so a generation-guard fix that is a no-op when generation never changes should leave them passing unmodified, but every one of them exercises the exact code paths (removePending set/clear, removeStatus write, structuralWritePending read) the fix touches and must be re-run, not skipped.

findings.title: PRIMARY blast radius #2 — page.roster-deactivate.spec.ts (member-deactivate flow, both single- and two-collective)
findings.detail: 1288 lines. Single-collective blocks exercising deactivatePending directly (same 'no-op when generation is constant' analysis as above, but every one touches the exact flag/finally the fix rewrites): describe ':194 two-step confirm' (:195-233), ':235 refusal while grant held' (:236-360, fail-closed paths through the SAME try/catch/finally), ':362 inactive surface' (:386-568, includes ':430' second-tap-while-reinstate-in-flight and ':512'/':536' deactivate-with-panel-open reload interplay — these touch the SAME outer try block the deactivatePending finally sits in), ':570 fail-LOUD' (:571-732), and — most load-bearing — describe ':734 #286 armed pair through in-flight deactivate' (:745-1058): `:745` blocker-read in flight, `:782` WRITE in flight (disabled+aria-busy, double-tap refused), `:829`/`:863` CANCEL-during-held-read/write is inert, `:900` second row cannot steal the arm slot, `:942`/`:985` refusal/failure leave pair armed. This block owns the file's `deferred<T>()` helper (:735-743) — the exact release-controlled-promise pattern to reuse for a new #287 regression test that holds deactivateMember/deleteSection itself (see next finding). THEN describe ':1060 (B) #259 — in-flight inactive-panel loads must not outlive a collective switch' is the file's ONLY cross-collective block: `:464` 'switching collectives clears the panel' (single assertion, not mid-write), and the three deterministic-race tests `:1137`/`:1168`/`:1212` — IMPORTANT: `:1168` ('a POST-DEACTIVATE panel reload that settles after a switch writes NOTHING') calls the real handleDeactivateConfirm and switches mid-flight, but deactivateMemberMock resolves immediately (`mockResolvedValue(undefined)`, beforeEach :150) — only loadInactiveRosterMock is held (via holdInactiveLoads(), :1103-1112). This test therefore exercises the window where deactivatePending is STILL true post-switch (because the finally is nested after the held panel-reload await) but asserts only that inactiveRows/inactive-member-row rendering stays clean — it never asserts on deactivatePending's own reset-to-false, on B's deactivate-trigger disabled state after switching, or on deactivateActionError/deactivateRefusal leaking across collectives. It is the closest existing test to #287's actual defect but does not cover it.

findings.title: No existing test combines 'hold the remove/deactivate WRITE itself' with 'switch collectives mid-write' — the fixture pieces exist separately and are directly composable
findings.detail: Three reusable house-method pieces already exist in this repo and can be spliced together for the new #287 regression test(s), rather than reinvented: (1) collective-switch driving — page.roster-arrange-stale-success.spec.ts's `switchToOtherChoir(container)` (:201-208) which does `selectedCollectiveDbStore.set('other-choir')` then waits for collective B's own rows to render, plus its `setAuthedWithTwoCollectives()` (:123-140) and disjoint fixture builders `treeA()/treeB()`/`rowsA()/rowsB()` (:95-121) — OR the near-identical duplicate in page.roster-deactivate.spec.ts's #259 block (:1081-1098, :1124-1133); (2) held-write mocking — page.roster-deactivate.spec.ts's own `deferred<T>()` (:735-743, generic resolve/reject capture) used already to hold deactivateMemberMock/listDeactivateBlockersMock, or page.roster-arrange-stale-success.spec.ts's inline `new Promise<void>((res) => { release = () => res(); })` pattern (:214-220) applied there to reorderMock/reparentMock; (3) `flush()` (`new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 0))`) appears in both files to let a released promise's continuation run before asserting. A new spec (or a new describe block in page.roster-deactivate.spec.ts / page.roster-arrange-crud.spec.ts) needs only to hold deleteMock/deactivateMemberMock (not just the panel-reload/reorder mocks) and switch mid-flight — no new fixture or mocking machinery is required. page.roster-arrange-stale-success.spec.ts's own header comment (lines 1-20) explicitly documents this as 'the house method for timing proofs' and cites #259's construction, confirming it is the established idiom to reuse for #287's regression coverage too.

findings.title: Secondary/low-risk touches — remove flow only, single-collective, gating not pending-state
findings.detail: page.roster-empty-remove.spec.ts (344 lines): describe ':245'/':300' assert section-remove-<id> `disabled` based on whether a section is empty (canDelete gating via sectionErrors.ts), not on removePending/structuralWritePending in-flight state, and never switch collectives — very low risk of needing changes, listed for completeness since they assert on the same button/testid. page.roster-indent.spec.ts:1220 queries `section-remove-${id}` but only asserts tabindex presence, unrelated to pending state.

findings.title: No other callers/importers of the two handlers or the two flags — blast radius is confined to +page.svelte and its own spec files
findings.detail: handleRemoveSection (:1602) and handleDeactivateConfirm (:868) are page-local, non-exported functions; grep of the whole file shows their only invocations are their own onclick bindings at :4392 and :3456 respectively — no other component or route imports them. `grep -rn "removePending|deactivatePending" --include=*.ts --include=*.svelte .` (excluding the page itself) hits only comments inside page.roster-deactivate.spec.ts:716 and page.roster-arrange-crud.spec.ts:726 — no code elsewhere references either flag by name (tests assert on rendered `disabled`/`aria-busy` DOM attributes and testids, never on the flags directly, since neither is exported). DeleteTrigger.svelte (src/lib/components/DeleteTrigger.svelte), the shared component the delete trigger renders through, has no internal pending state of its own — it takes disabled/aria-busy as plain props, so it needs no changes and has no tests of its own to move.

findings.detail:
File: src/routes/roster/+page.svelte (4637 lines total). Verified 2026-09-08 against current main (repo confirmed to be mvox-app.git). Grep terms per task: `Pending`, `pending`, `inFlight`, `Busy` — no `inFlight`/`Busy`-named flags exist in the file; all in-flight state uses the `*Pending`/`pending*Id` naming idiom.

| # | Flag | Decl. line | Set at | Cleared at (success/finally) | Route-load `reset` clears it? | Clearing `finally`/settle generation-guarded? | Verdict |

**Scope-fence summary for #287:** Rows 4 (`deactivatePending`) and 8 (`removePending`) are the two flags named in #287's done-when — fix only these two (reset in the route-load `reset` callback; generation-guard their `finally` blocks, reusing the `#260` idiom already correctly present in `performReorder`/`performReparent`'s success branches).

**Flags sharing the identical gap shape, named here per the scope fence for their own issue (NOT fixed in #287):**
- `reinstatePending` (row 6, decl. 1038) — same defect: not reset on switch, `finally` (1076) unconditional.
- `reorderPending` (row 9, decl. 2027) — `finally` clauses at 2142 and 2300 unconditional (its success-path announcements are already correctly guarded, unlike rename).
- `renamePending` (row 10, decl. 2367) — same `finally`-unguarded gap as the others, PLUS the success announcement at line 2438 (`renameStatus = m.roster_section_renamed(...)`) is itself ungated by generation — the one flag in this sweep where even the #260 idiom is missing on the happy path, not just the settle. Also note NONE of the five rename-related state vars are cleared by the route-load `reset` callback at all.
- `deactivateActionError` (row 5) — not itself a `Pending` flag, but its two writer sites (`handleDeactivateConfirm` catch at 944, `handleReinstate` catch at 1071) are unguarded by generation, so a stale-collective failure can paint an alert into the new collective's row list; worth naming alongside the pending flags since it's the same failure-class root cause (async settle races a collective switch, write comes after the switch's reset already ran).

findings.title: Axis 1 — collective switch mechanics: soft-nav, single choke point, two UI triggers
findings.detail: The `+page.svelte` component instance is NEVER destroyed/remounted on a collective switch — `/roster` is one route, and switching collectives changes only `?collective=<db>` plus store state, resolved via SvelteKit's client-side `goto` (soft nav). This is why `$state` like `removePending`/`deactivatePending` genuinely survives across a switch (confirmed, not speculative). Two UI paths converge on ONE data path: (a) `selectCollective(db)` (src/lib/collectives/store.ts:174-186), called only from src/routes/collectives/+page.svelte:36, sets `selectedCollectiveDbStore` + localStorage + does `goto(...)` to write `?collective=`; (b) any other URL-driven change to `?collective=` (deep link, browser back/forward, manual edit) is picked up by the root layout's reactive effect `urlCollectiveDbStore.set(page.url.searchParams.get(COLLECTIVE_URL_PARAM))` (src/routes/+layout.svelte:57-58). Both funnel into `selectedCollectiveStore` (src/lib/collectives/store.ts:77-97, URL wins over persisted pick over first-in-list), which the roster page reads via `$derived($selectedCollectiveStore)` (+page.svelte:64) and an `$effect` (+page.svelte:233-242) that re-invokes `routeLoad.loadForSelected()`. The shared machine (src/lib/loading/routeLoad.ts:83-141) bumps a `generation` counter and computes `isSwitch` by comparing `current?.db ?? null` against the last-loaded db (routeLoad.ts:96-101) — so ANY of the above trigger paths is normalized to the same `reset({isSwitch})` call the page's `reset` callback already handles (+page.svelte:116-164). `removePending` (declared :1600, set true :1659) and `deactivatePending` (declared :787, set true :884) are the only two flags in that reset callback's neighborhood NOT cleared — everything else structurally analogous (`pendingRemoveId` :129, `pendingDeactivateId`/`deactivateRefusal`/`deactivateActionError` :132-134) already is. What survives across a switch by design: `sections`/`rows` are wholly replaced by the new load; `expandedIds` is cleared (:173, :215, :222); the inactive panel is cleared only `if (isSwitch)` (:159-163, deliberately not on a same-db refresh).

findings.title: Axis 1 (mechanism) — WHY both a switch-reset AND a generation-guarded finally are both needed, not either/or
findings.detail: Both handlers already gate re-entry synchronously: `if (structuralWritePending) return;` in handleRemoveSection (+page.svelte:1608, where `structuralWritePending = reorderPending || renamePending || removePending` at :2393) and `if (deactivatePending) return;` in armDeactivate/handleDeactivateConfirm (:814, :869). So while collective A's write is still in flight and its flag is stuck true, collective B's SAME controls (once admin re-resolves — see axis 3) are inert/disabled from the first render — this is exactly the issue's 'disabled from load' symptom, not a double-submit. Adding the two flags to `reset()` fixes that immediately at switch time. But A's stale promise can settle LATER, after the user has legitimately started a NEW write on B (which set the flag true again for B's own row). Both `finally` blocks currently write their flag unconditionally (removePending :1717 inside a `finally` at :1716-1719; deactivatePending :969 inside a `finally` at :968-982) — a late A-settle would then clobber B's genuinely-in-flight flag back to false, re-enabling B's controls mid-write and reopening a real double-submit window. This is precisely the failure mode the `#260`/generation-guard idiom (`const g = routeLoad.generation;` captured pre-await, `if (!routeLoad.isCurrent(g)) return;`/`if (g !== routeLoad.generation) …` at resume) already used pervasively elsewhere on this page — see :1647/:1702/:1706 (handleRemoveSection's own reconcile), :947/:951/:954 (deactivate's inactive-panel reload), :1012/:1016/:1019, :1058/:1062/:1065, :1202+, :1349+, :2106+, :2229+, :2435+ — closes.

findings.title: Axis 1 (implementation-relevant gap) — handleDeactivateConfirm has no entry-level generation capture to guard its outer finally with
findings.detail: handleRemoveSection already captures `const g = routeLoad.generation;` at :1647, BEFORE its `try`/`await`, so guarding its `finally` (:1716-1719) with the same `g` is a straight reuse. handleDeactivateConfirm does NOT: its only `const g = routeLoad.generation;` is at :947, deep inside the `try`, AFTER `await loadForSelected()` already ran (deliberately captured late per the comment at :934-946, scoped narrowly to the inactive-panel reload at :948-957). That inner `g` is the wrong capture point/wrong variable for guarding the outer `finally` at :968-982 (which sets `deactivatePending = false` at :969 and does focus work at :979-982) — a naive reuse of the existing `g` would either shadow-collide or read a post-loadForSelected (already-bumped) generation, defeating the guard on the success path specifically. The finally-guard needs its OWN generation captured at function entry (mirroring handleRemoveSection's :1647 placement, i.e. before `deactivatePending = true;` at :884).

findings.title: Axis 5 / cross-cutting — the success-path live-region write itself is unguarded, and is the SOLE cross-collective leak from a stale removeStatus write (data-safe otherwise)
findings.detail: handleRemoveSection's success branch (inside the `try`, before the `finally`) does three things after `await deleteSection(cfg, id)` with NO generation check at all: `sections = removeSectionNode(sections, id)` (:1668), `pendingRemoveId = null` (:1670), and `removeStatus = m.roster_section_removed({ name })` (:1684) — this is exactly the mechanism behind the issue's stated consequence 'the success path announces A's removal into B's live region.' Traced the blast radius of an unguarded late settle: `pendingRemoveId = null` is idempotent (already null post-switch-reset); `sections = removeSectionNode(sections, id)` is a safe no-op on B's tree because Entu entity ids are scoped to their own database and collectives are switched by `db` (verified src/lib/loading/routeLoad.ts:96-99, src/lib/collectives/store.ts `Collective.db`), so A's section id cannot collide with any of B's — no data corruption. The ONLY live cross-collective leak is `removeStatus`, written into the sr-only `role="status" aria-live="polite"` region at :3642-3649 (`data-testid="roster-section-remove-status"`). Also notable: the comment block at :138-139 claims `removeStatus`/`pageCreateStatus`/`renameStatus` are reset in `reset()` 'matching' `reorderStatus`/`recordStatus' — verified FALSE from source: only `reorderStatus` (:122) and `recordStatus` (:151) are actually cleared in `reset()`; `removeStatus` (declared :1591), `pageCreateStatus` (:1817), and `renameStatus` (:2375) are cleared only at the START of their own handler, never on a collective switch. This means the fix satisfying done-when #3 ('a live-region announcement can never name an action performed in a different collective') requires guarding the SUCCESS branch's `removeStatus` write with the already-captured `g`/`isCurrent(g)` at :1647 — not merely adding `removePending`/`deactivatePending` to `reset()` and guarding the `finally` blocks. This is the same flow (handleRemoveSection), not a different pending flag, so it stays inside the two-flags scope fence, but it is a THIRD guard site beyond 'clear the flag on switch' + 'guard the finally' that the done-when text implies without naming explicitly.

findings.title: Axis 2 — locale coverage: all message keys reachable from the two handlers exist in en/et/lv/uk; NO new message needed
findings.detail: Enumerated every i18n key written into a live region (role=status or role=alert) by handleRemoveSection / armDeactivate / disarmDeactivate / handleDeactivateConfirm and confirmed presence in all four bundles (messages/en.json, messages/et.json, messages/lv.json, messages/uk.json) by direct lookup: `roster_section_removed` (success, +page.svelte:1684, region :3642-3649) — present all 4. `roster_section_remove_not_empty` / `roster_section_remove_failed` (failure, :1712, region role=alert :3752-3763) — present all 4. `roster_member_deactivate_confirm_prompt`, `roster_member_deactivate_confirm`, `roster_member_deactivate_cancel`, `roster_member_deactivate` (static button/prompt copy, :3448-3477) — present all 4. `roster_deactivate_refused_admin` / `roster_deactivate_refused_librarian` (refusal, role=alert :3481-3500) — present all 4. `roster_member_deactivate_failed` (catch-path, role=alert :3502-3514) — present all 4. No key was found missing in any locale. Neither `removePending` nor `deactivatePending` has, or needs, a dedicated message key of its own — both flags only ever drive boolean `disabled`/`aria-busy` attributes (see axis 5), never live-region TEXT. The #287 fix is pure state-management (clear-on-switch + generation-guard); it introduces zero new i18n surface, confirming the issue's own parenthetical ('none, because guarding means suppressing').

findings.title: Axis 3 — rights tiers: both controls are admin-gated (deactivate additionally self-excluded); adminStore resets to 'loading' on every switch, temporarily hiding controls, but the stale flags surface again once re-resolved
findings.detail: Section-remove controls render only under `{#if admin === 'admin'}` (e.g. +page.svelte:3627 for the header trigger tree; the confirm/cancel pair at :4384-4394 is nested inside that same admin-gated block). Deactivate controls render only under `{#if admin === 'admin' && row.personId !== selected?.personId}` (:3429) — admin-only AND never on the viewer's own row (self-deactivate is structurally unrenderable, matching the comment's 'done-when 7' citation at :3430-3432). `admin` is `$derived($adminStore)` (:65). Traced adminStore's switch behavior in src/routes/+layout.svelte: `resetAdmin()` (src/lib/nav/adminStore.ts:8-10, sets state to 'loading') fires synchronously on every `selectedColle ctiveIdentityStore` change (+layout.svelte:176-184), then `resolveAdmin(cfg, selected.personId)` (async) resolves the NEW collective's rights independently — confirmed from src/lib/nav/adminStore.ts:20-27 this is a per-DATABASE-ENTITY `_owner`/`_editor` read (#161 ruling), with no inheritance/propagation across collectives; a viewer can legitimately be admin on A and not on B, or vice versa. Consequence for #287: during the 'loading' window the admin-gated controls literally unmount (admin !== 'admin'), which HIDES the stuck-pending symptom transiently; if the viewer is NOT admin on B, the bug never surfaces at all (no controls to be stuck-disabled). The bug only manifests for a viewer who is admin on BOTH A and B: once `resolveAdmin` re-settles to 'admin' for B, the controls remount, and — absent the #287 fix — render pre-disabled because `removePending`/`deactivatePending` are still true from A's unresolved write. So rights-gating narrows WHO can hit this bug but does not itself close the gap; it only adds a race window before the stale-disabled state becomes visible.

findings.title: Axis 4 — invite-created vs auto-provisioned persons: no differentiation found in either flow (verified from source, not just absence of a search hit)
findings.detail: handleRemoveSection operates on a SECTION entity (`deleteSection(cfg, id)`, id being a section id from `sections`, not a person) — provenance of a person is categorically inapplicable to this flow. handleDeactivateConfirm calls `deactivateMember(cfg, row.memberId)` -> `flipMemberStatus(cfg, memberId, 'archived', fetchImpl)` (src/lib/roster/memberLifecycle.ts:44-46, 73-97): the write reads/overwrites only the member entity's `status` property via the atomic-overwrite wire (GET current status value-id -> ONE POST pairing old id with new value); there is no read of, or branch on, any invite/auto-provision marker anywhere in this call chain. `RosterRow` (src/lib/roster/rosterData.ts:174-232) carries `memberId`, `personId`, `name`, `email`, `sectionIds`, `dbEntityId`, and profile-name fields — no `provenance`/`source`/`invited` field exists on the type at all. Grepped the whole roster page and memberLifecycle.ts for `provenance`/`invite`/`autoProvision` — the only hits are unrelated doc comments (memberLifecycle.ts:57's 'reinstate WITHOUT a fresh invitation', rosterData.ts:88's unrelated `inviteData.ts` reference). Conclusion: neither `removePending` nor `deactivatePending`'s flow branches on how the person/member came to exist; the #287 fix needs no provenance-conditional logic.

findings.title: Axis 5 — accessibility: exact live-region declarations, and the DISTINCT (non-text) a11y risk for deactivatePending
findings.detail:
removeStatus's region: `
{removeStatus}
` at +page.svelte:3642-3649, mounted from first render per the page's own stated contract ('a live region announces only CHANGES to its contents' — comment :3637-3641) alongside sibling regions of the same shape: `roster-reorder-status` (:3611-3613), `roster-section-create-status` (:3655-3662), `roster-section-rename-status` (:3667-3674), `roster-member-record-status` (:3680-3687) — all `role="status"`/`aria-live="polite"`/`sr-only`, all populated only on SUCCESS (failures use `role="alert"` elsewhere). There is NO equivalent success-text region for deactivate — a successful deactivate reloads the whole roster (`await loadForSelected()` at :927) and the row simply disappears; no message key is ever written to announce deactivate success. deactivateRefusal's alert (`member-deactivate-refused-{memberId}`, role="alert", :3481-3500) and deactivateActionError's alert (`member-deactivate-failed-{memberId}`, role="alert", :3502-3514) are BOTH already gated on `pendingDeactivateId === row.memberId` in their render condition (:3481, :3502) — since `pendingDeactivateId` is already cleared unconditionally by `reset()` (:132), these two alerts CANNOT stand against a foreign-collective row post-switch already, by construction, independent of the #287 fix. So deactivatePending's ONLY accessibility exposure is non-textual: `aria-busy={deactivatePending}` and `disabled={deactivatePending}` on the confirm button (:3453-3454) and cancel button (:3463) — if the flag is stuck true after a switch, B's remounted confirm button would render `aria-busy="true"` and disabled from first paint, falsely signaling an in-progress operation to assistive tech that never actually started on B. This is a STATE-attribute staleness, not a stale-TEXT-announcement, and needs no live-region clearing beyond the flag fix itself — there is no stale text to additionally blank out for the deactivate side (unlike removeStatus, which per the finding above needs the success-write itself generation-guarded, since it holds actual stale TEXT that reset() never clears).
